title: timetable-ab: controlled cross-language comparison of abstract-structure cost (raw data, 7 languages, 14 specifications)
description:
A pre-registered, reproducible cross-language experiment on the cost of abstract structures (macros vs. table-driven dispatch). One frozen specification (5 ops) implemented from scratch in seven languages by isolated agents, plus fourteen follow-up specifications: scale, product fan-out, expansion-time validation, body-level inlining, iteration/maintenance, two-agent hand-off, a 30-op crossover, and a skill-pack A/B.

What is included: every run artefact (543 files), the 36 invariants and their go-red proofs, mutation scores with their sample-size bounds, the twelve mutation floors, and a 2318-line append-only chronicle that records nineteen occasions on which the measurement apparatus itself was wrong — each with the symptom, the discovery, and the rule it produced.

What is excluded: compiled binaries (*.exe), build caches, and machine-local temporary files. No personal data is included.

Headline results that were not expected: (1) physical line count differs by 4.05x between two implementations of the same specification while non-blank non-comment characters differ by only 7.6% — line count measures formatting, not language; (2) macro-based dispatch loses on authoring cost at this scale (11460 vs 5933 characters for the same 15 ops); (3) no positive crossover point was observed; (4) a skill-pack intervention showed no detectable effect across a 6-run A/B, because the executing model's error rate was already near zero (ceiling effect).

Intended use: replication of the measurement protocol, reuse of the mutation-testing gate, and empirical grounding for work on benchmark validity in LLM code generation.
notes: Generated 2026-10-24. The chronicle in reports/ is append-only; nothing was deleted when a conclusion was refuted, only annotated with its scope.
